newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen staying cautious before Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen staying cautious before Greenspan.

text.p: Trading in Germany's DAX share index was expected to remain cautious before the resumption of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony on Wednesday, dealers said on Monday.

Dealers said they could not rule Greenspan giving further signals that could be interpreted as making the case for a rise in U.S. interest rates after last week's warning over lofty stock prices and inflation risks.
"Overall the market is on hold and is looking with some trepidation towards America," said one trader. The IBIS DAX index traded down 2.30 points at 3,258.74 by 1610 GMT.
Volumes were, aside from a handful of stocks, relatively small in the German market all day on Monday, dealers said.
Deutsche Telekom shares rose 83 pfennigs to 33.71 marks in IBIS as dealers said buying, especially from U.S. investors, had been prompted by a series of positive analyst studies recently.
